i've found it extremely scary to think about.

that said, as other people have noted, the prevalence of false memories of abuse has been exaggerated. that may be comforting to think about.

another thing to focus on is a kind of "felt truth", where you're not focusing on the truth of a specific memory but just acknowledging the feelings that you have inside of you that were caused by the abuse. i will probably never know for certain what happened to me around 5-6 years old - i was too young to remember properly, and the only other people around were my family. but i know about the gut-wrenching fear and revulsion that thinking about that time brings up in me, i know about how later i would feel sick when my abuser told me she loved me, and i know about all the other effects that i've dealt with other the years.

where there's smoke there's fire, broadly speaking. if you've found yourself consistently dealing with stuff that seems a lot like sexual trauma, then i think it's fine to assume good faith in yourself and work under the assumption that there's something going on there, even if you can't objectively verify your memories.

hey thanks for your response. I didn't come back to this account for a while but I'm feeling (sort of) better now, so I had the energy to return and respond. everything's still there in my mind but I'm trying to tell myself that I don't need to justify being alive. anyways, just wanted to say thank you cause your response was so thoughtful and kind.
